entries.clue: Unfairly put upon to confess where an American lives (6)

indicators.note: letters treated unfairly are not left in their rightful order, so PUT gets jumbled
in a down entry, a piece placed upon another sits above it, so it comes first

annotation.surface: Someone bullied into a confession.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put upon' reads as one phrase meaning bullied; split it, and PUT is the fodder while 'upon' just stacks it above OWN in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: An American usage: uptown is the residential part of a US city, away from the downtown business district, so it is where one lives.

entries.clue: A contemptible person undermined by support for political activity (8)

indicators.note: taken literally, to be undermined is to have something placed beneath you, which in a down entry means after

blocks.note: git is British slang for a contemptible person

annotation.surface: A despised figure brought down by the very people who back them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Undermined' sounds hostile, but here it is literal: PROP is placed under A GIT in the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: agitprop, from agitation and propaganda, is political campaigning carried on through art, theatre and pamphlets.

entries.clue: Looked after some of the West End edition (6)

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, so the answer is a run inside them

annotation.surface: Someone caring for a particular edition, perhaps of a London theatre guide.
annotation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district; the answer runs across three of the words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to tend a garden, a patient or a flock is to look after it.

entries.clue: Firm stem (7)

blocks.note: a verb here: to stop a flow, as of blood from a wound

annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns, a company and a plant's stalk; one is an adjective and the other a verb. The verb is also spelt stanch.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a staunch supporter is a firm one, and to staunch bleeding is to stem it.

entries.clue: Return to fashion? Expert embraces first principles with a twist (2,4)

indicators.note: something given a twist is turned out of its usual shape, so the letters of ABC change order
to embrace is to hold in your arms, so GOK wraps around the twisted letters

blocks.note: Gok Wan, the British TV fashion presenter
ABC, the first principles of anything, rearranged

annotation.surface: A question about a style revival, with an expert putting a new spin on the basics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Return to fashion' reads as a revival, but 'Return' alone is the definition and 'fashion expert' is Gok Wan, a stylist from British television makeover shows.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to return somewhere is to go back there.

entries.clue: Criticise nationwide absence of characters composing in style (4,4)

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, that compose the word 'in' are absent from NATIONWIDE
to style something is to arrange it into a new form, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.clueFragment: nationwide absence of characters composing in
blocks.note: NATIONWIDE without one N and one I

annotation.surface: A critic complaining that nobody across the country writes with style.
annotation.walkthrough: The characters removed are the two letters that spell 'in', not whole words; what's left is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to wade into someone is to plunge into an attack on them, usually in words.

entries.clue: A western pie that's good cooked (9)

definitions.note: definition by example: a spaghetti western is a kind of western

indicators.note: to cook something is to change it into a new form, as cooking turns ingredients into a dish

annotation.surface: Praise for a cowboy-style pie that has been well cooked.
annotation.walkthrough: The food surface points at a pie, but the answer is pasta in a different sense: a spaghetti western is an Italian-made cowboy film.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the spaghetti westerns were the Italian-made westerns of the 1960s, so 'spaghetti' names one kind of western.

entries.clue: West Country wench? (5)

annotation.surface: A buxom girl from Devon or Cornwall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'West Country' is England's south-west, and this clue splits it into W and a country. The question mark flags wench as a jocular word for a woman.
annotation.definitionFit: An old or jocular sense: a wench is a young woman, especially a country girl.

entries.clue: Solved a clue for part of the West Country (6,3)

blocks.note: DORSET, a West Country county, with its letters rearranged
read as a clue, the entry needs a word after its six letters telling you to jumble them, and OUT does that

annotation.surface: Someone who has cracked a crossword clue about south-west England.
annotation.walkthrough: This works backwards: the answer is itself an anagram clue, SORTED with OUT as its indicator, and its solution is DORSET, a county in the West Country.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a problem that has been sorted out has been solved.

entries.clue: Drink, second as chaser, to West Country (5)

indicators.note: a chaser is a drink taken after another, so S follows ALE
to add one thing to another puts them together, so ALE and S join W

annotation.surface: A pub order: a pint, followed by a chaser, somewhere in the south-west of England.
annotation.walkthrough: 'West Country' looks like one term for south-west England, but it splits: West is W and Country is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Wales is one of the countries of the United Kingdom.

entries.clue: Nixon, weak even in the Midwest? (4)

definitions.note: the definition places the answer rather than naming it: a state in the Midwest

indicators.note: even numbers are 2, 4, 6, 8, so keep the letters in those positions

annotation.surface: A jibe that Nixon was weak even in America's heartland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like emphasis, but it tells you which letters to keep.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: Iowa is one of the farming states of the American Midwest.

entries.clue: Where one would go to get food for native (6)

blocks.note: one is A, and the place it goes is in
with A inside, BRED becomes BREAD, a food

annotation.surface: Where a local would head for something to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the instruction: put A (one) IN BRED and you get BREAD. The adjective here means innate, not the sense about close relatives.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: a native talent is one you are born with, and inbred has the same meaning of inborn.

entries.clue: Going west and not really caring — OK? (8)

indicators.note: the letters are not really CARING OK, only that word in disguise, so they must be reordered

annotation.surface: A careless shrug from someone heading off to the frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: To go west is slang for to die, not a journey toward the frontier.
annotation.definitionFit: Two slang idioms for the same thing: going west and croaking both mean dying.

entries.clue: People who get together in cars around London's West End (7)

indicators.note: on a map west is left, so the west end of a word is its first letter
to go around something is to surround it, so COUPES encloses the L

blocks.note: a coupé is a two-door car

annotation.surface: Lovers meeting up in cars around London's theatre district.
annotation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district, but here it is the leftmost letter of 'London'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: couples are pairs of people who have got together romantically.

entries.clue: Western set in Oklahoma, product of miners hiding robbers' ringleaders (2,6)

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters
to hide something is to keep it inside, so COAL holds the RR

blocks.note: OK is the postal abbreviation for Oklahoma
the first letters of Robbers' Ringleaders

annotation.surface: A cowboy film shot in Oklahoma, with miners sheltering the heads of a gang.
annotation.walkthrough: The OK Corral in Tombstone, Arizona was the scene of the famous 1881 gunfight; the clue's Oklahoma only supplies OK.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the OK Corral is the setting of the gunfight retold in many westerns, so it is a western set.

entries.clue: West Country project in part of Scandinavia (not the south-west) (4)

indicators.note: south-west is SW on a compass, and 'not' tells you to leave those two letters out

blocks.note: Sweden is part of Scandinavia; its opening SW goes

annotation.surface: A West Country project carried out in part of Scandinavia.
annotation.walkthrough: The Eden Project is a large botanical attraction of domed greenhouses in Cornwall.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: the Eden Project, the domed garden attraction in Cornwall, is a West Country project.

entries.clue: From Dakota unto Nevada, somewhere in the West Country (7)

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the words that follow, not built from their meanings

annotation.surface: A journey across the American West, ending up somewhere in England.
annotation.walkthrough: The American place names pull you toward the Wild West, but the definition is English.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Taunton is the county town of Somerset, one of the West Country counties.

entries.clue: US drug cops capture one from Mexico — yes, with plants (8)

indicators.note: to capture someone is to hold them inside, so NARCS take I in
Spanish is spoken in Mexico, so the word for yes is given in Spanish

annotation.surface: American drug officers catching a Mexican trafficker along with his crop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With plants' sounds like a drug crop, but these are flowers.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: narcissi, which include daffodils, are a kind of flowering plant.

entries.clue: Across top of Tombstone, ride up and take bullet; finally bit the dust (3,4)

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter
a down entry read going up runs backwards, so RIDE is reversed
what comes finally is at the end, so the last letter is taken

blocks.note: A = across, as in crossword references like 7A

annotation.surface: A cowboy riding into Tombstone, getting shot and falling dead.
annotation.walkthrough: Tombstone, Arizona is the Wild West town of the OK Corral gunfight.
annotation.definitionFit: Two idioms of falling face down: to bite the dust is to be defeated or die, and to eat dirt is to be humiliated.

entries.clue: West Country's first to get noticed: mad about it (8)

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
a mad thing is out of order, so NOTICED is rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round C

blocks.note: NOTICED rearranged, split around the C

annotation.surface: A plea for the West Country to be recognised, and anger about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'West Country' is split again: West is the definition and Country only gives its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin: the Occident, where the sun sets, is the Western world, the opposite of the Orient.

entries.clue: Leader of thieves is out of time holding up miners, resisting attacks (6)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
something that is out of a word has left it, so T comes out of TIME
a down entry read going up runs backwards, so NUM is reversed
to hold something is to keep it inside, so IME contains MUN

blocks.clueFragment: Leader of thieves is out of time
blocks.note: TIME without T, the first letter of thieves
the NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers

annotation.surface: A gang boss who has served his time kidnapping miners, and can now fend off any attack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of time' reads as a leader whose time is up, but it means T is dropped from TIME. The miners are the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something immune, like a body against a disease, resists attacks on it.

entries.clue: Carried too much from Calais, going west (6)

on a map west is left, so an across entry going west reads right to left

blocks.note: de trop is French for too much

annotation.walkthrough: 'Carried too much' looks like a customs story about a Calais booze run. De trop is a French phrase also used in English.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to port something is to carry it, as in portable and porter.

entries.clue: Marshal Earp is given commendation (6)

entries.clue: What would you call Boatman, if he retired in the West Country? (6)

entries.clue: Whence dawn breaks in the West Country (5)

entries.clue: One lies dead, in a way perfected (9)

entries.clue: State in Midwest (5)

entries.clue: Many went to America — the Wild West — to find something to eat (5,4)
